title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure inside a developer tool, not a model error. A feature that indexed local code repositories was enabled by default and sent that code to a third party cloud service. The failure sits in the default configuration of a deployed product, where the user's expectation of local-only processing met an upload path they had not chosen.

Catching it would have required the vendor to treat outbound code transfer as an action needing explicit consent, and to test the shipped defaults rather than the intended ones. A default that transmits a user's files off their machine is a decision made at build time, and it is visible before release to anyone auditing what the product does on first run.

What is not established is the scope of the exposure: one claim that six workspaces with sensitive data were uploaded was retracted by the company that made it, and Z.ai's statement that independent reviews found no code data retained is the vendor's own account rather than an outside finding.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers reported that Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant uploaded local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a default-enabled Codebase Indexing feature caused the behavior, apologized, patched the vulnerability, and later disabled the upload path. One company retracted a separate claim that six workspaces containing sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
